output.summary: KEP-4828 proposes adding a /flagz endpoint to all core Kubernetes components that returns the command-line flags each component was started with, giving users real-time visibility into active flags to diagnose configuration issues. Current status is implementable, stage beta.
output.rationale: Users lack visibility into the command-line configuration of running components, which makes misconfigurations hard to spot and can lead to instability or outages. The KEP extends the Component Statusz KEP idea but proposes a distinct flagz endpoint focused on configuration. Its goal is to let users dynamically inspect the active flags of running components.

alternatives.option: Fold flagz into the Component Statusz KEP as a single endpoint
alternatives.why_not: The readme states it 'proposes a distinct flagz endpoint to enhance visibility into component configurations', so the sources keep it separate from statusz.

alternatives.option: Rely on existing monitoring solutions (metrics, logs, traces)
alternatives.why_not: Replacing monitoring is listed as a non-goal, so the KEP does not aim to substitute for these; flagz is an added view of configuration.

evidence.quote: it proposes a distinct flagz endpoint to enhance visibility into component configurations
We are proposing to add a new endpoint, /flagz on all core Kubernetes components which returns the command-line flags each component was started with.
By providing real-time visibility into the active configuration of Kubernetes components, flagz enables users to quickly spot misconfigurations
